title: About.
lead: A software developer in Gurgaon, India, building backend services and the platforms they run on. Currently an Executive on a client deputation through Quess Corp Limited, and looking for software developer, backend, and DevOps roles.
paragraphs: I write Go services and the infrastructure that runs them, and lately the Next.js interfaces some of that work needs on the other side. Most of what I find interesting sits at the seam between those two: a service is not finished when it returns the right response, and a page is not finished when it renders — both are finished when there is a repeatable way for them to reach production and an honest signal when they stop behaving.

The thing I keep coming back to is that infrastructure and applications both run on claims nobody checks. A controller advertises self-healing. A chart declares a liveness probe. A tool claims it can detect a data leak. In most repositories those are sentences, not results, because verifying them costs an afternoon and no reviewer is going to ask. The gap between a configured guarantee and a tested one is where outages, and false confidence, live.

So the case studies here are written the other way round. Each one states a decision, what it cost, and the cases it does not cover. Where I could not verify something against the repository, it is not on the page — which is why there is less here than there could be.
Outside that client work: I read source when documentation disagrees with behaviour, which happens more than it should.
